sources.rank_basis: TypeScript's own documentation site (typescriptlang.org/docs/handbook), official docs of the project.
MDN Web Docs under developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/, a curated secondary reference, not the spec.
v8.dev/blog/ is the V8 project's engineering blog (the most specific match is the /blog/ path, not the project's docs).
Node.js official API documentation (nodejs.org/api), saved page is the v26.13.1 docs with the feature's version history.
github.com/<org>/<repo>/issues/ path: a community feature request and its comments, unvetted.
README of the TC39 class fields proposal repository, the originator's own publication of the concept; not an issues/discussions/pull path, though not pinned to a tag.

claim_checks.claim: `private` and `protected` are enforced only during type checking. Runtime lookups, and bracket notation even during type checking, still reach the member: it is "soft private".
claim_checks.page_says: Like other aspects of TypeScript’s type system, private and protected are only enforced during type checking.
claim_checks.note: The same section also says bracket notation is allowed during type checking and calls these fields soft private.

claim_checks.claim: `#` fields stay private after compilation and have no bracket-notation escape hatch: they are "hard private".
claim_checks.page_says: JavaScript’s private fields (#) remain private after compilation and do not provide the previously mentioned escape hatches like bracket notation access, making them hard private.

claim_checks.claim: When compiling to ES2021 or lower, TypeScript replaces `#` with `WeakMap`s. The handbook notes that these runtime privacy checks will degrade performance.
claim_checks.page_says: When compiling to ES2021 or less, TypeScript will use WeakMaps in place of #. … Note that these added privacy checks during runtime could affect performance.
claim_checks.note: The WeakMap downlevel part is supported. The handbook says 'could affect', the doc says 'will degrade' (stronger modal). The handbook's note is about hard runtime privacy mechanisms in general (closures, WeakMaps, private fields), not specifically about the downlevelled output.

claim_checks.claim: Private elements are not properties. They cannot be enumerated, deleted, proxied, or reached through `Object` methods, and `structuredClone()` copies them like public fields.
claim_checks.page_says: For this reason, structuredClone() does not clone private elements … they cannot be proxied, enumerated, deleted, or interacted with using any Object method.
claim_checks.note: The first sentence is supported; the structuredClone part states the opposite of the page, which says private elements are not cloned.

claim_checks.claim: Reading a `#` field from an object whose class did not declare it throws a `TypeError`. `#x in obj` checks for it without throwing.
claim_checks.page_says: If you access a private element from an object that doesn't have the element, a TypeError is thrown … use the in operator to check
claim_checks.note: The page's example shows `if (#x in obj)` returning true or false.

claim_checks.claim: V8 9.4 moved class-field initialization, including private fields, onto its inline-cache fast path. Before that it went through slower runtime calls.
claim_checks.page_says: The first issue has been fixed in V8 v9.7 … Before v9.7, V8 always used a costly runtime call for class field initializations.
claim_checks.note: Wrong version: the page gives v9.7, not 9.4 (the doc's own frontmatter also says V8 ≥ 9.7). The claim also drops the qualifier that the IC is used only when the initialization pattern is predictable enough, otherwise V8 falls back to a runtime call.

claim_checks.claim: An injected collaborator (port, clock, logger) → `private readonly x` constructor parameter, because a `#` name cannot be a parameter property.
claim_checks.page_says: That this is not possible is a bit surprising
claim_checks.note: The 2020 feature request and its comments say `#` parameter properties are not possible; the saved text does not show the issue's current state. Grounded, but the source is Rank 6 in a role 3 section (KB-15 breach). The handbook [^1] Parameter Properties section lists only public, private, protected or readonly as the modifiers that create one.

claim_checks.claim: Object wrapped in a `Proxy`: `#` access does not go through the proxy, because private elements cannot be proxied.
claim_checks.page_says: they cannot be proxied, enumerated, deleted, or interacted with using any Object method.

claim_checks.claim: Target ES2021 or lower: `#` becomes `WeakMap` lookups, because TypeScript downlevels it.
claim_checks.page_says: When compiling to ES2021 or less, TypeScript will use WeakMaps in place of #.

claim_checks.claim: Working around it with `--experimental-transform-types`: the flag is removed in Node 26.0.0, so code meant to run unbuilt keeps injected collaborators as `readonly #field`s assigned in the constructor.
claim_checks.note: Listed under v26.0.0 in the page's history table; the page also says parameter properties require transformation and error under type stripping. The ExperimentalWarning on Node 24.22 is a local re-test and was not checked; the recommendation is the doc's own inference from these facts.

claim_checks.claim: Type stripping is stable (stability 2) since Node 24.12.0 and 25.2.0; no warning since 24.3.0; Node ignores `tsconfig.json` and needs `.ts` extensions in relative imports, because Node only deletes types.
claim_checks.page_says: v25.2.0, v24.12.0 | Type stripping is now stable. … Node.js ignores tsconfig.json files … file extensions are mandatory in import statements
claim_checks.note: The history also lists v24.3.0 and v22.18.0 for 'no longer emits an experimental warning', and 'Stability: 2 - Stable'.

violations.evidence: C3 overstates [^1]: the handbook says the added runtime privacy checks 'could affect performance', the doc says they 'will degrade performance' and ties the note to the WeakMap downlevel only.
C4 contradicted by [^2]: MDN says structuredClone() does not clone private elements; the doc says it copies them like public fields.
C6 contradicted by [^3]: the V8 blog dates the class-field initialization fix to V8 v9.7, the doc says 9.4 (and contradicts its own applies-to: V8 ≥ 9.7).
The 'Where each form fits' table row 'A # name cannot be a parameter property ✅[^5]' cites a Rank 6 source (GitHub issue) in a role 3 section, which allows ranks 1–4.
[^6] (TC39 class fields proposal) is never cited in the body; its entry says it backs How it works 2, which cites only [^1].
States 'Verified: 10 claims (✅)', but the body carries 11 ✅ marks (7 in How it works, 4 in Edge cases).

'On a native ES2022+ target, reading and creating # fields costs the same as public fields' (and the Takeaway 'measured cost is nil') carries no mark or citation and rests on one local measurement (Node 24.22, V8 13.6). [^3] says class-field initialization was much slower before V8 v9.7, so the scope 'native ES2022+ target' is wider than the evidence.

The role 3 section mixes a role 5 decision table ('Where each form fits') into the mechanism steps. No section holds role 2 (parts and relations); the doc uses its own template rather than the research headings, so this was mapped by content and scored as one weak section.

patch_instructions.action: Item 3: replace 'The handbook notes that these runtime privacy checks will degrade performance.' with 'The handbook notes that hard runtime privacy mechanisms (closures, WeakMaps, private fields) could affect performance.' per [^1]: 'Note that these added privacy checks during runtime could affect performance.'

Item 4: replace 'and `structuredClone()` copies them like public fields' with '`structuredClone()` does not clone them, and `Object.freeze()` and `Object.seal()` have no effect on them' per [^2]: 'structuredClone() does not clone private elements, and Object.freeze() and Object.seal() have no effect on private elements.'

Item 6: change 'V8 9.4' to 'V8 v9.7 (included in Node.js 18.0.0)' and add 'when the initialization pattern is predictable; otherwise it falls back to a runtime call', per [^3]: 'The first issue has been fixed in V8 v9.7' and 'Before v9.7, V8 always used a costly runtime call for class field initializations.'

'Where each form fits', injected-collaborator row: replace ✅[^5] with ✅[^1] and reword to 'Parameter properties are created only with public, private, protected or readonly; a # name is not one of them', per the handbook's Parameter Properties section. Move the [^5] feature request (2020, status not shown) to ## Edge cases or ## Trade-offs as context.

Either cite [^6] in How it works item 2 (the proposal README says 'It's impossible to access the private field from outside of the class, unless there is some explicit code to expose it') or delete the [^6] entry.
Recount the ✅ marks after the fixes above and update the count (currently 11 in the body, stated as 10).

Scope the performance sentence to the evidence: 'On V8 ≥ 9.7 (Node ≥ 18) with a native ES2022+ target, …', and point to the Worked example measurement; [^3] can back the narrower statement that Node.js benchmarks showed no regressions after switching back to private fields. Apply the same scope to the second Takeaway.
Optionally move the 'Where each form fits' table under its own reference heading (role 5) so How it works holds only the mechanism steps.
